 Print Yamuna foam clouds Chhath celebrations: AAP, BJP trade barbs over cleaning claims (PTI photo) NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party on Monday claimed that the BJP governments in Delhi and at the Centre had failed to clean the Yamuna, accusing them of making false claims about the river's condition. The remarks came as thousands of Purvanchali devotees gathered at its ghats to celebrate Chhath Puja amid "toxic foam". Taking aim at the Rekha Gupta-led government, the Arvind Kejriwal-led party claimed that the BJP's promises of cleaning the Yamuna had fallen flat. "The Rekha Gupta government's blatant lie about cleaning the Yamuna is exposed right here!" AAP wrote on X. Watch Dead Fish In Yamuna: BJP Accuses AAP Of Staging Incident, Kejriwal's Party Hits Back In another post, sharing a picture purportedly showing a Chhath devotee performing rituals amid toxic foam floating on the river, the AAP said, "Today, all the BJP’s claims about its four-engine government cleaning up the Yamuna have been exposed!" "Chhath devotees had to celebrate the great festival of Chhath like this amid toxic foam," Kejriwal's party added. In the video the caption read, "not AI, this is Yamuna on Chhath." Delhi AAP chief Saurabh Bharadwaj also posted the same video with caption: "Today’s video under BJP rule." Congress attacks BJP over Yamuna pollution during Chhath
 The Congress also targeted the BJP-led government over the condition of the Yamuna during Chhath Puja, sharing pictures of toxic foam floating on the river and accusing the ruling party of failing to clean it. In a post on X, the Congress alleged that the government had misled people with claims about cleaning the Yamuna, pointing to the river's condition during the festival. "Modi and the BJP have lied through their teeth about cleaning up the Yamuna—these photos are proof," the party said. It further alleged that women devotees were forced to enter "toxic, foamy water" to perform Chhath rituals, accusing the BJP of betraying hundreds of thousands of devotees. "Modi and the BJP have betrayed hundreds of thousands of devotees and committed a grave sin," the Congress said, adding that "Mother Yamuna and Chhathi Maiya will never forgive Narendra Modi and the BJP." BJP defends Yamuna cleanup, targets previous AAP govt
 The BJP, however, stood by its claims that the Yamuna had become cleaner under its government, while turning the spotlight on the previous AAP regime. Hitting back at the opposition, the ruling party said, "The same Yamuna where Chhath was banned is now more than half clean in just 2 years, and Delhi’s Sanatani CM celebrates Chhath in it." Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta also took to X to highlight the scale of this year's celebrations, saying the festival was being celebrated with grandeur across the capital after decades. "Decades later, Delhi is witnessing such a transcendent, wondrous and magnificent celebration of the great Chhath festival. From the sacred banks of Mother Yamuna to nearly 1,400 Chhath ghats, the songs of Chhath, the devotion of hundreds of thousands of worshippers and the worship of the Sun God have bathed the entire capital in the colors of faith," she wrote.  "To the people from Purvanchal, I would like to say that we made every effort to ensure that Chhath Mahaparv gets celebrated in a divine and grand manner; forgive me if anything was lacking and I will try to make even better arrangements next year," CM told reporters. Chhath Puja is a four-day Hindu festival dedicated to the worship of Surya Dev, and Chhathi Maiya. Devotees observe the festival to express gratitude to the Sun for sustaining life on Earth and seek blessings for good health, prosperity and longevity. This year's celebrations began on November 13 and concluded on Monday, November 16, with Usha Arghya, the ritual offering of prayers to the rising Sun. Poll Vote & Share your view
